chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

And the mothers breastfeed their children. He (the Imam) said: As long as the child is in the period of breastfeeding, he is equally shared between the parents. When he is weaned, the father has more right to him than the mother. If the father dies, the mother has more right to him than the agnates (male relatives). If the father finds someone to breastfeed him for four dirhams, and the mother says 'I will not breastfeed him except for five dirhams,' then he has the right to take him from her, unless it is better for him and more gentle for him to leave him with his mother.
ai.seo_question: What are the Shia Islamic rules for child custody after weaning and in case of the father's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential hierarchy of child custody (hadanah) in Shia law, emphasizing the father's primary right after weaning while acknowledging the mother's superior claim over agnates (asabah) upon the father's death. It introduces a practical economic dimension, allowing the father to reclaim custody if the mother demands disproportionate breastfeeding fees, provided such separation serves the child's best interest (maslaha). This ruling reflects the interplay between paternal authority and maternal care, grounded in the principle of the child's welfare.
